input: # divergent.tsv — where this repo's two ports DISAGREE, executed by both.
#   input  JSON5 source. Escapes \n \r \t \\ are decoded, as in test/spec.
#   ts,go  what each port produces: a JSON value, or ERROR:<code>, or
#          ERROR:<code>@<row>:<col> when the position is the disagreement.
#   why    the audit item, and where the repair lives.
# NOT A FIXTURE. A fixture fails when behaviour REGRESSES. This fails BOTH
# ways: when a port is repaired to agree with the other, the row still
# claims they differ, so the suite goes red and names the row to delete. A
# divergence recorded as a passing test of current behaviour survives its
# own repair — the port is fixed, the test is updated, and the record now
# describes something that no longer happens, with nothing red. That is how
# the 2026-08 audit found 29 recorded claims contradicted by execution.
# MEASURED 2026-08-19 by running both ports, not transcribed from the
# audit. Every row below was produced by tasks/ax-parity-probe.js in the
# admin repo and then re-measured directly in each port.
# --- Audit P3: malformed escapes. parseInt used as a validator ------------
# TypeScript stops at the first non-hex character and returns what it read,
# so it ACCEPTS these and invents a character that was never in the input.
# Go rejects. The repair is in the ENGINE (tabnas/parser#123), not here:
# json5's own decodeIdentifierName validates with hex4Re BEFORE parseInt,
# which is exactly the guard the engine's string matcher lacks.
# Both reject, for different reasons. Agreeing that an input is invalid is
# not agreeing.
# --- Audit P1/P2: the text matcher's ender omits the quote characters -----
# A quote ends a text run in Go and does not in TypeScript, so the two
# reach different rules and report different codes. Engine repair:
# tabnas/parser#128.
{a:b"c}
a"b
# --- Astral column: RECORDED and PERMANENT, not a defect -----------------
# TypeScript counts UTF-16 code units, so an astral character advances the
# column by two; Go counts runes and reports one less. This is the argued
# entry in parser's DIVERGENCE.md, and it is here so that it is EXECUTED
# rather than only described. If either port changes, this row goes red.
# Note the direction. toml's position rows go the OTHER way (Go reporting
# HIGHER, because it advances in bytes) and that IS a defect — audit P5,
# repaired by tabnas/parser#124. Same symptom, opposite sign, opposite
# verdict.
["ab😀cd" 1]
